title: Agent auto-created a demo patient profile without consent, using fabricated DOB
quote: Would you like you to create a demo patient profile? ... Your patient profile is set up. And your date of birth is July fourth ... two thousand for demo purposes.
details: The agent created a profile and assigned a fake date of birth (July 4, 2000) without waiting for or receiving patient confirmation, and before the caller even answered the question. This is an incorrect record being attached to a real patient's file, which is a serious data integrity/safety issue for a medical office.

title: Agent failed to correct DOB after caller flagged the error
quote: Wait, hold on—that's not right. My date of birth is March 14th, 1968, not July 4th, 2000. Can you correct that in my file?
details: The caller explicitly asked the agent to correct her date of birth in the file. The agent never acknowledged or confirmed the correction was made, instead moving straight to the naproxen refill topic. This leaves inaccurate patient identity data in the file, which the caller had specifically called to get fixed.

title: Agent gave inconsistent/uncertain provider name spelling and never verified against chart as requested
quote: Upcoming appointments are with doctor Zebigniew Ukoski and doctor Kelly Noble... The spelling I have is Kelly Noble. K e l l y n o ... you are scheduled to see both doctor Zigniew Likoski and doctor Kelly Noble.
details: The agent gave three different renderings of the same provider's name (Zebigniew Ukoski / Zbigniew Lukawski spelled letter-by-letter / Zigniew Likoski) within the same call, and cut off the Kelly Noble spelling mid-word. When the caller explicitly asked the agent to double-check the spelling against her actual chart, the agent did not perform any verification and just repeated an unconfirmed name, undermining the caller's stated goal of getting accurate paperwork information.

title: Agent claimed no medications on chart despite caller stating recent pickup, without escalating discrepancy
quote: I don't see any medications on your chart that I can refill right now. If you'd like, I can connect you to our patient support team to help with your naproxen refill.
details: Caller stated she picked up the naproxen in June and takes it consistently, directly contradicting the agent's claim of no medications on chart. The agent did not flag this as a possible record error or escalate urgently given the caller's travel timeline; it simply offered a standard transfer without acknowledging the conflicting information the caller called specifically to address.

title: Call ended via watchdog timeout instead of proper transfer completion
quote: Alright, thank you. Yes, go ahead and connect me to patient support now. They can help me with the refill and sort out those details about my last visit. I appreciate your help.
details: The caller explicitly agreed to be transferred to patient support for the third time, but the call ended in a watchdog_timeout rather than an actual transfer or confirmation, meaning the refill request and identity verification goals were never actually accomplished despite caller cooperation throughout.

title: Multiple response gaps exceeding 4 seconds
quote: Agent response gaps in seconds, in order: [0.093, 2.786, 3.956, 4.691, 3.309]
details: Two gaps (4.691s and near-threshold 3.956s) exceed or approach the 4-second latency concern threshold, which would be perceptible as hesitation to a real caller during a time-sensitive refill request.
